newsitem.title: USA: ARCO says waiting to see impact of Burma sanctions.
newsitem.headline: ARCO says waiting to see impact of Burma sanctions.

text.p: U.S. oil major Atlantic Richfield Co said Tuesday that it is waiting for details of the unilateral U.S. sanctions against the Burmese military regime to assess the impact on its two projects in the country.
"We're waiting to see the regulations to see exactly what the government will do. We will abide by that policy," said ARCO spokesman Albert Greenstein.
Los Angeles-based ARCO is one of a number of U.S. companies still doing business in Burma and one of two key oil and gas concerns active in the country, along with Unocal Corp.
The Secretary of State is due to make a formal announcement Tuesday at noon on sanctions against the Burmese military government, citing human rights abuses for the action.
ARCO has invested "several million" dollars in two offshore exploration blocks, M-9 and M-7, drilling for natural gas, according to Greenstein.

The M-9 block exploration encountered gas, but up to this point there has been no confirmation of a commercial find. The second block has seen no drilling yet, with a seismic exploration program recently completed.
ARCO acquired the lease rights for the blocks in 1995 and 1996, Greenstein said.
The U.S. sanctions are not expected to affect existing projects, though it is unclear whether those which have not yet reached development stage will be allowed to proceed.
"If this is applied, the two (ARCO) fields would be outside the sanctions," Greenstein said.
